changes.comment: createHttpTransport takes an optional authProvider (McpOAuthClientProvider, the SDK's OAuthClientProvider under this package's name) for MCP servers that require OAuth 2.1. The SDK is given a forwarding wrapper, a different object from the consumer's provider. The interactive steps (state, saveCodeVerifier, redirectToAuthorization) run only inside connectMcpSession; on a later call, the SDK's background reconnect of the event stream, or close they are refused and the operation fails 'unauthorized'. redirectToAuthorization is also refused for a URL that is neither https: nor http: on a loopback host. The 'unauthorized' reason gains resourceMetadataUrl, the validated resource_metadata URL from the endpoint's WWW-Authenticate challenge (an http(s) URL with no username or password). An OAuth error from the authorization server now classifies as 'unauthorized'. HTTP-error and OAuth-error text no longer reaches a failure message: an 'unauthorized' failure, or one from an HTTP or OAuth error, reads as its kind and status (e.g. "unauthorized (HTTP 401)", "transport (HTTP 500)"), because a server may repeat a credential. 'tool-error' and 'protocol' messages still carry server text by design, and the SDK's other auth errors can name a server-chosen URL. Static headers are now applied by the package's egress wrapper, only to requests for the MCP endpoint's origin (overriding a same-named header there, as before), and never to the authorization server or any other origin; the SDK is no longer given them. Without a consumer fetch, a request carrying static headers refuses redirects (globalThis.fetch would carry them to any origin); with a guarded fetch its default 'reject' holds, and 'validate-each-hop' carries a static header across a redirect unless it is listed in sensitiveHeaders. createHttpTransport refuses a static header named twice in different letter cases, and fails with fixed text when building the transport throws (an invalid header, or an authProvider member that throws). Static headers are copied when createHttpTransport is called; later changes to the caller's record have no effect. A fetch getter that throws fails createHttpTransport with fixed text.
